text:
Devon Toews has been one of the best players on the Avalanche this season, and the outside world has noticed: Sports Illustrated, Heavy.com and Denver Sports 104.3 The Fan all ran his bounce-back in the same week. He has 7 goals and 21 points in 23 games on 22 minutes a night, after scoring 3 goals all of last season.

The process behind it is real. Colorado gets about 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, more than 10 points better than when he sits. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the best defensemen at getting to the slot and setting up teammates last season, so the playmaking isn't new.

The goals are the part to treat carefully. He's scored 7 on 3.4 expected, shooting 17% when our range for him sits nearer 7%, and the team has scored 11.1 more goals than expected with him out there. Evolving-Hockey also notes he plays beside very strong teammates. The minutes (up to almost 24 a night lately) and the play driving should stay. The goal pace is the part our numbers say rarely lasts.
